chunks: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar in Qum narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Yousuf narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Eesa narrated to us, from Abdurrazak, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah; and Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi said: And he narrated this to us from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Zayd al-Shahham.

He said: I asked Abu Abdillah: 'Which is better, al-Hasan or al-Husayn?' He said: 'The virtue of the first of us attaches to the virtue of the last of us, and the virtue of the last of us attaches to the virtue of the first of us; so each has his virtue.' I said to him: 'May Allah make me your ransom, expand upon the answer for me, for by Allah I do not ask you except as one seeking the truth.' He said: 'We are from one tree, Allah created us from one clay. Our virtue is from Allah and our knowledge is from Him. We are Allah's trustees over His creation, the callers to His religion, and the veil between Him and His creation. Shall I add more to you, O Zayd?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Our creation is one, our knowledge is one, our virtue is one, and we are all one before Allah.' I said: 'Inform me of your number.' He said: 'We are twelve - thus - around the Throne of our Lord, glorified and exalted, at the beginning of our creation. The first of us is Muhammad, the middle is Muhammad, and the last of us is Muhammad.'
ai.seo_question: What is the theological status of the Twelve Imams regarding their unity and number according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) elucidates the ontological unity of the Twelve Imams, describing them as emanating from a single essence and serving as Allah's trustees (amānā) and veils (ḥujaj) between the Divine and creation. This narration, found in al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, reinforces the doctrine of the fixed number of Imams by linking them to the Throne, while highlighting their shared lineage and divine knowledge. The statement that the first and last share equal merit underscores the continuity of the Imamate from Muhammad ibn Ali to Muhammad al-Mahdi.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (16) Ali bin al-Husayn narrated from Muhammad bin Yahya al-Attar from Muhammad bin Hassaan ar-Razi from Muhammad bin Ali al-Kufi from Ibraheem bin Muhammad bin Yousuf from Muhammad bin Eessa from Abdurrazak from Zayd ash-Shahham that Abu Abdullah (as) had said (the same, which had been also narrated) by Muhammad bin Hassaan ar-Razi from Muhammad bin Ali al-Kufi from Muhammad bin Sinan that Zayd ash-Shahham had said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as): “Who is better; al-Hasan or al-Husayn?” He said: “The virtue of the previous one of us joins the next one of us and the virtue of the next one of us joins the previous one. Each one of us has his virtue.” I said: “May my soul be sacrificed for you! Would you explain the answer more to me because I look for the truth?” He said: “We are from one tree. Allah has created us from one clay. Our virtue and knowledge are from Allah. We are the deputies of Allah over His people, the propagandists for His religion and the means between Allah and His people. Do I say more to you O Zayd?” I said: “Yes!” He said: “Our creation is the same. Our knowledge is the same. Our virtue is the same and we all are the same before Allah.” I asked: “Would you tell me how many you are?” He said: “We are twelve ones. So has been determined around the Throne at the beginning of the Creation. The first of us is Muhammad. The middle is Muhammad and the last of us is Muhammad.”
